  "summary": "S1 — Fact: the target is an existing Node.js project with an in-memory user store, described by README.md, and an HTTP server at src/server.js; discovery leads are that README, server, store, package configuration, and existing tests, with their contents yet to be verified. S2 — Outcome: add name filtering, pagination, and tests to the existing user list endpoint in this project; discovery must first establish the route, response format, existing conventions, test setup, and any documented API contract, then determine query parameters, matching and pagination behavior, and invalid-input handling, which block implementation and tests. Assumption: preserve existing behavior and use repository conventions where the contract is silent; do not add authentication, persistent storage, or a new interface. API clients consume the endpoint; discovery must establish any existing client identity, shared in-memory state, its lifetime, visibility, and runtime-provided behavior before deciding whether they affect the change; the default rules out adding identity or cross-session persistence. The isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, when the change becomes visible there; any deployed endpoint reflects the outcome only after release."
